notes: This sheet continues a sentence about contraction forming a générisation. It promises to return to the structure of an extension as a fibre product of extensions, names a hom of générisation on fundamental groupoids, and announces a transitivity property for a composite. Display (104) contains two unlabelled single rightward arrows between underlined G, G prime and G double prime. The following groupoid diagram was begun and cancelled before any right-hand target was supplied.

No proof, theorem, or completed transitivity identity is present on this page. No mathematical claim was independently checked or used as a proved background result; the reading relies on ink and recurrence within this sheet only.

The exact authorial forward reference is “On reviendra sur la structure de cette extension, comme un produit fibré d’extensions, un peu plus bas…”. The cancellation of Plus and of the unfinished diagram are visible revisions. The two retained unsure marks are transcriptional uncertainty, not authorial question marks.

The first superscript of gamma has been left locally uncertain. The cancelled diagram has a clearly visible star associated with its upper object and a prime after the second G. Its two Pi letters have a top bar and two legs; they are not product signs or lowercase pi. All readable objects and both arrow directions are retained.

The word générisation on line 10 is heavily retraced at its beginning, but no separate readable underlying word or independently attached insertion can be distinguished. No extra deletion or insertion has been invented there.

The pale bottom-left 80 is a source foliation. Its authorship cannot be established from this sheet; it remains as margin{80} rather than being silently asserted to be the author’s manuscript numbering. There is no date.

Every required crop was made once from original coordinates with LANCZOS enlargement, autocontrast, and mild sharpening, then visually inspected. No crop was rotated. No OCR, recognition software, external source, other page, or TeX compilation was used. The complete draft retains C where the ink supports it; C/H macro-only differences and H’s editorial note are not source-text changes.
